title: CO HB1263: Conversational Artificial Intelligence Service Operator Requirements

obligations: Use commercially reasonable methods or generally accepted methods to estimate the age of account holders or users and not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that an account holder or user is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).

On and after January 1, 2027, if operator knows account holder or user is a minor, clearly and conspicuously disclose that the minor is interacting with artificial intelligence that is artificially generated and not human, with persistent visible disclaimer, intermittent audio disclaimer, or at beginning of each interaction and at least once every three hours in continuous interaction (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(a)).
Not provide minor account holder or minor user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with intent to encourage increased engagement (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(b)).

Institute technically feasible measures to prevent service from producing textual, visual, or aural depictions of explicit sexual conduct; producing an intimate digital depiction; generating a statement that minor should engage in explicit sexual conduct; or engaging in erotic or sexually explicit interactions with minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(c)).

Institute reasonable measures to prevent service from formulating, structuring, or optimizing a response that simulates emotional dependence or isolation from real-world supports, including preventing explicit claim human or sentient, statement simulating romantic companionship, or role-playing adult-minor romantic relationship (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(d)).
Implement a protocol to prohibit service from engaging in explicit sexual conduct with a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(e)).
Implement a protocol for service to stop engaging in response to a user prompt regarding explicit sexual conduct with a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(f)).
Comply with part 13 of article 1 regarding protecting privacy and data of a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(g)).

Offer tools for minor account holder or minor user to manage privacy and account settings, including control over retention of prior interactions for personalization and use of personal data for training; offer tools for parent or guardian to manage minor's privacy and account settings (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(h)).

On and after January 1, 2027, clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that service is artificial intelligence, at beginning of first interaction each day, at least once every three hours in continuous interaction or persistent disclosure, and in response to user prompts (Sec. 6-1-1708(3)).

On and after January 1, 2027, implement a protocol for service to respond to user prompt regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm, including user referral to a crisis service provider such as suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis service, but not including law enforcement agency, and escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators (Sec. 6-1-1708(4)).

On and after July 1, 2027, annually report to attorney general's office: number of crisis service provider referral notifications in preceding calendar year; protocols implemented to detect, remove, and respond to instances of suicidal ideation or self-harm; protocols to prevent service response about suicidal ideation or self-harm actions; and any additional metrics necessary as determined by attorney general (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(a)).
Ensure annual report does not include identifiers or personal information about a user (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(b)).
Use evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation or self-harm for purpose of creating report (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(d)).
prohibitions: Shall not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that an account holder or user is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).

Shall not provide minor account holder or minor user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with intent to encourage increased engagement with a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(b)).

Shall not use any term, letter, or phrase in advertising, interface, or outputs of a conversational artificial intelligence service that states that any output data provided by the service is being provided by, endorsed by, or equivalent to services provided by a licensed health-care professional, a licensed legal professional, a licensed, certified, or registered mental health professional, or a qualified dietitian as described in section 6-1-707(1)(b) (Sec. 6-1-1708(5)).

body_html:
Passed 2026-05-29. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Creates duties for operators of conversational artificial intelligence services, including age estimation, disclosures that the service is AI, protections for minor account holders and users against sexual content and emotional dependence, a suicide and self-harm crisis protocol, and annual reporting to the attorney general. It defines key terms and excludes many categories of software from the definition of conversational artificial intelligence service.

Who it applies to

  • Operators of conversational artificial intelligence services, meaning a person, partnership, corporation, or entity that develops and makes publicly available a conversational artificial intelligence service or offers one to a consumer (Sec. 6-1-1701(15.5)(a)). Mobile application stores and search engines are not operators solely because they provide access (Sec. 6-1-1701(15.5)(b)).

Effective date

August 12, 2026, if adjournment sine die is on May 13, 2026; if a referendum petition is filed, the act or affected part will not take effect unless approved by the people at the November 2026 general election and then takes effect on the date of the official declaration of the vote by the governor (Sec. 3).

Key definitions

  • conversational artificial intelligence service: an artificial intelligence system that is accessible to the general public and that primarily simulates human conversation and interaction through adaptive textual, visual, or aural communications; excludes listed software applications, web interfaces, or computer programs (Sec. 6-1-1701(3.5)(a), (b)).
  • explicit sexual conduct: has the meaning set forth in section 13-21-1502(7); does not include evidence-based medical information or factual descriptions of reproductive health care (Sec. 6-1-1701(10.5)).
  • intimate digital depiction: has the meaning set forth in section 13-21-1502(10) (Sec. 6-1-1701(12.5)).
  • minor: a consumer under eighteen years old (Sec. 6-1-1701(15.3)).
  • operator: a person, partnership, corporation, or entity that develops and makes publicly available a conversational artificial intelligence service or offers one to a consumer; does not include a mobile application store or search engine solely because it provides access (Sec. 6-1-1701(15.5)).
  • self-harm: intentional self-injury, with or without the intent to cause death (Sec. 6-1-1701(16.5)).
  • visual depiction: has the meaning set forth in 18 U.S.C. sec. 2256(5) (Sec. 6-1-1701(18)).
  • account holder: a consumer who has or opens an account or profile for the purpose of using a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 6-1-1708(1)(a)).
  • minor account holder: an account holder who is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(1)(b)).
  • minor user: a user of a conversational artificial intelligence service who an operator has knowledge is a minor by using commercially reasonable methods or generally accepted methods to estimate the age or age range of a user (Sec. 6-1-1708(1)(c)).

Obligations

  • Use commercially reasonable methods or generally accepted methods to estimate the age of account holders or users and not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that an account holder or user is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).
  • On and after January 1, 2027, if operator knows account holder or user is a minor, clearly and conspicuously disclose that the minor is interacting with artificial intelligence that is artificially generated and not human, with persistent visible disclaimer, intermittent audio disclaimer, or at beginning of each interaction and at least once every three hours in continuous interaction (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(a)).
  • Not provide minor account holder or minor user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with intent to encourage increased engagement (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(b)).
  • Institute technically feasible measures to prevent service from producing textual, visual, or aural depictions of explicit sexual conduct; producing an intimate digital depiction; generating a statement that minor should engage in explicit sexual conduct; or engaging in erotic or sexually explicit interactions with minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(c)).
  • Institute reasonable measures to prevent service from formulating, structuring, or optimizing a response that simulates emotional dependence or isolation from real-world supports, including preventing explicit claim human or sentient, statement simulating romantic companionship, or role-playing adult-minor romantic relationship (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(d)).
  • Implement a protocol to prohibit service from engaging in explicit sexual conduct with a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(e)).
  • Implement a protocol for service to stop engaging in response to a user prompt regarding explicit sexual conduct with a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(f)).
  • Comply with part 13 of article 1 regarding protecting privacy and data of a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(g)).
  • Offer tools for minor account holder or minor user to manage privacy and account settings, including control over retention of prior interactions for personalization and use of personal data for training; offer tools for parent or guardian to manage minor's privacy and account settings (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(h)).
  • On and after January 1, 2027, clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that service is artificial intelligence, at beginning of first interaction each day, at least once every three hours in continuous interaction or persistent disclosure, and in response to user prompts (Sec. 6-1-1708(3)).
  • On and after January 1, 2027, implement a protocol for service to respond to user prompt regarding suicidal ideation or self-harm, including user referral to a crisis service provider such as suicide hotline, crisis text line, or other appropriate crisis service, but not including law enforcement agency, and escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators (Sec. 6-1-1708(4)).
  • On and after July 1, 2027, annually report to attorney general's office: number of crisis service provider referral notifications in preceding calendar year; protocols implemented to detect, remove, and respond to instances of suicidal ideation or self-harm; protocols to prevent service response about suicidal ideation or self-harm actions; and any additional metrics necessary as determined by attorney general (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(a)).
  • Ensure annual report does not include identifiers or personal information about a user (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(b)).
  • Use evidence-based methods for measuring suicidal ideation or self-harm for purpose of creating report (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(d)).

Prohibitions

  • Shall not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that an account holder or user is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).
  • Shall not provide minor account holder or minor user with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals with intent to encourage increased engagement with a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(b)).
  • Shall not use any term, letter, or phrase in advertising, interface, or outputs of a conversational artificial intelligence service that states that any output data provided by the service is being provided by, endorsed by, or equivalent to services provided by a licensed health-care professional, a licensed legal professional, a licensed, certified, or registered mental health professional, or a qualified dietitian as described in section 6-1-707(1)(b) (Sec. 6-1-1708(5)).

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state penalties, enforcement authority, or a private right of action. It requires annual reports to the attorney general's office and requires the attorney general's office to post data from reports on its public website (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)(a), (c)).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organisation deploying a conversational AI service must determine whether it is an operator and whether the service falls within the definition or an exclusion (Sec. 6-1-1701(3.5), (15.5)).
  • It must estimate ages of account holders and users and cannot ignore clear evidence of minor status (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).
  • For known minors, it must provide AI disclosure, avoid unpredictable rewards, implement technical and reasonable measures to prevent sexual content and emotional dependence, implement protocols for explicit sexual conduct, comply with minor privacy law, and offer privacy tools to minors and parents (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(a)-(h)).
  • For all users, it must disclose AI status at first daily interaction, every three hours or persistently, and in response to prompts (Sec. 6-1-1708(3)).
  • It must implement a suicide and self-harm protocol with crisis referral not law enforcement and escalation procedures (Sec. 6-1-1708(4)).
  • It must not falsely represent outputs as from licensed health, legal, mental health, or dietitian professionals (Sec. 6-1-1708(5)).
  • It must annually report crisis referrals and protocols to the attorney general, without personal identifiers, using evidence-based methods (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)).

Notable exemptions

  • Conversational artificial intelligence service does not include software applications, web interfaces, or computer programs that are primarily designed and marketed for developer or researcher use; primarily designed to provide commerce-related or transactional assistance; designed to provide outputs relating to a narrow and discrete topic and cannot generate outputs related to sexually explicit conduct or depictions or maintain dialogue related to suicidal ideation or self-harm; primarily designed and marketed for commercial use by business entities for business operations, productivity, information analysis, internal research, training, or technical assistance; function as speaker and voice command interface or text interface and act as voice- or text-activated virtual assistant for consumer electronic device and cannot generate outputs related to sexually explicit conduct or depictions or encourage dialogue related to suicidal ideation or self-harm; used by a business solely for internal purposes; feature of video game limited to dialogue focused on video game and does not maintain dialogue on unrelated topics; feature of theme park or location-based entertainment limited to topics solely related to theme park or location-based entertainment and does not maintain dialogue about unrelated topics; used by covered entity or business associate under HIPAA or rendered to or provided on behalf of such entity; used by entity subject to Health Care Availability Act; educational tool designed primarily to support specific and limited instructional, administrative, accessibility, or student support purposes in a school setting and not designed to simulate emotional companionship or encourage emotionally dependent interaction; feature within another software application, web interface, or computer program where the other program is not the conversational AI service, not designed to simulate emotional companionship or encourage emotionally dependent interaction, and not a conversational AI service, including social media platform (Sec. 6-1-1701(3.5)(b)(I)-(XII)).
  • Operator does not include a mobile application store or search engine solely because the store or search engine provides access to a conversational artificial intelligence service (Sec. 6-1-1701(15.5)(b)).
  • Nothing in section 6-1-1708 limits an individual's ability to access information and resources under section 32 of article II of the state constitution and part 4 of article 6 of title 25; requires an operator to disclose trade secrets, confidential or proprietary information, or other information protected from disclosure by state or federal law; or authorizes content moderation practices inconsistent with the United States Constitution (Sec. 6-1-1708(7)).

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the product is a conversational artificial intelligence service under Sec. 6-1-1701(3.5) and whether the organisation is an operator under Sec. 6-1-1701(15.5).
  • Implement age estimation using commercially reasonable or generally accepted methods and do not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that a user is a minor (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)).
  • For known minor account holders and users, provide the required AI disclosure, avoid unpredictable rewards, institute technical measures to prevent sexual content and intimate digital depictions, institute reasonable measures to prevent emotional dependence, implement protocols for explicit sexual conduct, comply with part 13 minor privacy, and offer privacy tools to minors and parents (Sec. 6-1-1708(2)(a)-(h)).
  • For all users, provide the AI disclosure at the beginning of the first interaction each day, at least every three hours or persistently, and in response to prompts (Sec. 6-1-1708(3)).
  • Implement a suicide and self-harm protocol with crisis service referral not law enforcement and escalation procedures (Sec. 6-1-1708(4)).
  • Ensure advertising, interface, and outputs do not falsely represent output data as provided by, endorsed by, or equivalent to licensed health-care, legal, mental health, or dietitian professionals (Sec. 6-1-1708(5)).
  • Beginning July 1, 2027, prepare and submit annual reports to the attorney general's office with required metrics, no personal identifiers, using evidence-based methods (Sec. 6-1-1708(6)).

  (2) Minor account holders and minor users. AN OPERATOR SHALL
USE COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE METHODS OR GENERALLY ACCEPTED
METHODS TO ESTIMATE THE AGE OF ACCOUNT HOLDERS OR USERS. AN
OPERATOR SHALL NOT WILLFULLY DISREGARD CLEAR AND CONVINCING
INFORMATION THAT AN ACCOUNT HOLDER OR USER IS A MINOR. FOR
PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION, THE ESTIMATED AGE OR AGE RANGE OF A MINOR
ACCOUNT HOLDER OR USER IS CONSIDERED KNOWLEDGE OF THE MINOR'S
AGE. ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, IF AN OPERATOR KNOWS THAT AN
ACCOUNT HOLDER OR USER IS A MINOR, THE OPERATOR SHALL:

 (a) CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY DISCLOSE TO THE MINOR
ACCOUNT HOLDER OR MINOR USER THAT THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER OR
MINOR USER IS INTERACTING WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE THAT IS
ARTIFICIALLY GENERATED AND NOT HUMAN. THE DISCLOSURE MUST BE
PROVIDED IN RESPONSE TO USER PROMPTS REGARDING WHETHER THE
CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE IS ARTIFICIALLY
GENERATED AND NOT HUMAN AND MUST BE:

 (I) A PERSISTENT VISIBLE DISCLAIMER FOR A PRODUCT WITH A
SCREEN INTERFACE;

 (II) AN INTERMITTENT AUDIO DISCLAIMER FOR A PRODUCT WITHOUT
A SCREEN INTERFACE; OR

 (III) PROVIDED AT THE BEGINNING OF EACH INTERACTION WITH A
CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE AND MUST OCCUR AT
LEAST ONCE EVERY THREE HOURS IN A CONTINUOUS CONVERSATIONAL
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE INTERACTION;

 (b) NOT PROVIDE THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER OR MINOR USER
WITH POINTS OR SIMILAR REWARDS AT UNPREDICTABLE INTERVALS WITH THE
INTENT TO ENCOURAGE INCREASED ENGAGEMENT WITH A CONVERSATIONAL
ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE;

 (c) INSTITUTE TECHNICALLY FEASIBLE MEASURES TO PREVENT A
CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE FROM:

SEXUAL CONDUCT;

 (3) Consumer disclosures. ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, AN
OPERATOR SHALL CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY DISCLOSE TO A USER THAT
A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE IS ARTIFICIAL
INTELLIGENCE. THE DISCLOSURE MUST:

 (a) BE PROVIDED AT THE BEGINNING OF A USER'S FIRST INTERACTION
WITH A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE FOR EACH DAY
OF INTERACTION;

 (b) APPEAR AT LEAST ONCE EVERY THREE HOURS IN A CONTINUOUS
CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE INTERACTION OR
APPEAR AS A PERSISTENT DISCLOSURE VISIBLE TO THE USER; AND

 (c) BE PROVIDED IN RESPONSE TO USER PROMPTS REGARDING
WHETHER THE CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE IS
ARTIFICIALLY GENERATED AND NOT HUMAN.

 (4) Suicide and self-harm protocol. ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1,
2027, AN OPERATOR SHALL IMPLEMENT A PROTOCOL FOR A
CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE TO RESPOND TO A
USER PROMPT REGARDING SUICIDAL IDEATION OR SELF-HARM, WHICH

CRISIS SERVICE, BUT NOT INCLUDING A LAW ENFORCEMENT AGENCY, AND
ESCALATION PROCEDURES FOR REPEATED OR SEVERE CRISIS INDICATORS.

 (5) False representation. ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, AN
OPERATOR SHALL NOT USE ANY TERM, LETTER, OR PHRASE IN THE
ADVERTISING, INTERFACE, OR OUTPUTS OF A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL
INTELLIGENCE SERVICE THAT STATES THAT ANY OUTPUT DATA PROVIDED BY
